detailed_description: Live-action 1970s Shaw Brothers historical studio cinema, ancient Troy, saturated 35mm film colors, theatrical hard light, practical timber and stone sets. One enormous hollow wooden Trojan horse, visibly made from timber planks with the same golden bronze bands, mounted on the same four-wheeled timber platform. Its four rigid wooden legs never walk, its head never moves, and its wheels rotate only while pulled. One rectangular hinged hatch on its camera-facing belly and one wooden ladder. The Greek leader is the bearded short-dark-haired man in engraved bronze armor and a red cloak, with one sword sheathed at his right hip and no shield. His companion is the clean-shaven curly-dark-haired man in engraved bronze armor and a blue cloak, with one sword sheathed at his right hip and one round bronze shield strapped to his back. They use free hands to climb. Keep faces, hair, armor, cloak colors, equipment ownership and horse construction consistent. [Shot 1] Daylight. Continue the previous rightward tracking movement without a cut. The Trojan workers continue pulling the same wheeled wooden horse away from the gate into the paved central square. A stone fountain and two bronze braziers establish the square. The camera keeps the whole horse and platform visible. The hatch stays shut and all Greek soldiers remain hidden inside, invisible. overall_soundscape: Wooden wheels rumble, ropes creak, light fountain water and distant city ambience. No dialogue or music. non_diegetic_music: None.
